note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Human evaluation matters, criteria were defined and applied, revealing under-reporting and shifting use that motivate recommendations

nodes.name: Human evaluation is the gold standard
nodes.description: Human evaluation is still considered the gold standard for long-form generation where automated metrics work poorly, and increasingly also meta-evaluates LLM-judges.

nodes.name: Procedures lack standardization
nodes.description: Current human evaluation procedures lack standardization and operationalization, limiting validity, robustness, comparability and reproducibility.

nodes.name: 20 reportable criteria defined
nodes.description: The authors define 20 binary reportable criteria covering task definition, annotation operationalization, annotator information, and data analysis and interpretation, developed over four iterative codebook rounds.

nodes.name: Large-scale annotation of *CL papers
nodes.description: From 9.1k+ *CL papers (2023-2025), over 1,800 study long-form generation with human evaluation; 356 were sampled and 284 manually annotated in full.

nodes.name: Pervasive under-reporting
nodes.description: Most papers report evaluated dimensions (98%), number of annotators (77%) and number of samples (85%), but other criteria are reported far less often (Fig 1).

nodes.name: Guidelines and justification only about half
nodes.description: Only about 50% of papers give justification for the evaluation dimensions or the task guidelines shown to annotators.

nodes.name: Payment, IRB, statistics rarely reported
nodes.description: Payment information is reported in 29% of papers, IRB determination in 11%, statistical metrics in 9%, and none use power analysis for sample size.

nodes.name: IAA reporting is incomplete
nodes.description: Among papers with more than one annotator only 51% report inter-annotator agreement (46% overall).

nodes.name: Human evaluation proportion declining
nodes.description: Long-form generation papers rose from around 30% to 50% in 2025, but the proportion of all papers with human evaluation stayed around 20%.

nodes.name: LLM-judges widely adopted
nodes.description: Half of manually annotated papers use LLM-judges, and 20% of these use them for other dimensions without human evaluation.

nodes.name: Human meta-evaluation of LLM-judges rising
nodes.description: Papers using both LLM-judges and human evaluation for the same dimensions rose from 4% in EMNLP'23 to 30% in EMNLP'24 and 12% in EMNLP'25, without evident reporting improvement.

nodes.name: R1: Report core criteria succinctly
nodes.description: Authors should report the core reportable criteria for reproducibility, which can be done succinctly in a short passage.

nodes.name: R3: Hold human evaluation to higher standard
nodes.description: Because human evaluation increasingly serves as the standard for assessing LLM-judges, weak protocols introduce error downstream, demanding greater rigor and documentation.

isolated_nodes.name: Binary criteria annotated reliably
isolated_nodes.description: Binary questions yield the most reliable annotator judgments (81% agreement), versus 69% and 53% for other question types (Sec 4).

isolated_nodes.name: Heterogeneous demographics reporting
isolated_nodes.description: 29% of papers report no annotator demographics and 65% report no recruitment platform; among those that do, 50% recruit domain experts and 31% students (Sec 5).

structural_reasoning: Study design leads to findings of under-reporting and shifting practice, from which recommendations follow.
